body: ``` meta-expression First prototype for a links-network based reasoning playground. It accepts a human-language statement, generates selectable interpretations, formalizes the selected meaning when possible, evaluates computable fragments, and attaches evidence with provenance for non-computable claims. The implementation in this PR keeps the long-term direction documented in docs/REQUIREMENTS.md and docs/ROADMAP.md, while providing working library, CLI, microservice, and static web surfaces now. The text-formalization sub-system has its own auto-generated reference at docs/FORMALIZE.md (regenerated from JSDoc with npm run docs:formalize). ``` ``` alternative. For example, https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q2555318 is connected to https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q52701496 via https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Property:P910 So `automated reasoning` is clearly a context here. User needs ability to easy select between all possibilities, using something like drop down list, meaning on hover of the word, we should be able to change the result of disambiguating, so `reasoning` should be mappable to ``` https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q1156402 https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q484284 https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q484284 https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q1151406 https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q3478658 ``` Which themselves should be gathered using the search. We know that the common between them is `reasoning` word itself, may be we can also scan using other words that have similar meanings, yet the top match should be exact match. Also we need to check what is different about them, to what categories they belong, how we can choose between them. Meaning we should collect all categories/worlds/context for all alternatives. So in that specific case we now got: ``` Contexts Click a context to reinterpret the same text through that lens. No shared contexts inferred. Big-context categories Worlds and domains the text touches (Math, Geography, Star Wars, Genshin Impact, ...). The first item is the dominant world. No big-context categories detected. ``` These should be checkboxes, that should be autoselected (like top 5). Meaning we have for each words for example 10+ ways to intepret the word, and each way have some big categories/contexts that are connected directly or indirectly to them. Meaning for example we have at least 10% of words in the text, that include `computer science` or `automation` or similar. That means it can be on of the top categories, and can be preselected. So we use most commonly linked top categories as a hint for disambiguating all other words. Also on hover of each word in the result we should use some kind of 2 way tooltips one is for expressing the description of the word + its categories (it should come on top), and one is for drop down list + editor, if drop down list does not contain required item, so we should also be able to type manually Q/P id. Also word ``` formalize ``` Was not detected as https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q115492965 (but this item contains `to formalize` as one of its forms. Also `the` exists in `https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/the`, even if it does not exists in wikidata or wikipedia, we still use it in similar way. So the priority of disambiguating is like this: If exists as wikipedia article - use it, if not try wikidata, if not even there - wikitionary. Please make sure we use actual data in all places, and make our disambiguating as perfect as possible. Double check all other cased you can notice, carefully cover with tests each and every detail, make sure you tests can access cached version of wikipedia/wikidata/wiktionary API. So when testing in CI/CD, we don't load their servers too much. We should do it like this - we use real API, and record requests and responses, once we saw how it worked, we use that as snapshot for unit tests. Even better if we will be able to generate tests or parts of tests automatically by capturing everything in real API locally, and converting that to unit tests code, that will execute real code, but against recorded versions of API. So our API should be able to operate against cache/overrides or real API or both, and all of them. So we should be able with as many layers as we need. For easy data extension locally in rare cases, and for merging different APIs or data sources, and for automated testing against data snapshots recording saved in the repository as .lino files. Please use our issues, requirements, and other real data in the repository to produce as much examples for formalization as possible. So later we will be able to use our tool to fully formalize each and every statement in our own repository. We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions). Please plan and execute everything in a single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
